sentences.text: Theiophytalia was a herbivorous dinosaur belonging to the ornithischian class.
Its genus name means 'divine garden' and honors James Hutchinson Kerr, the man who found the fossil.
The partial skull discovered in 1878 is the only known fossil of this genus.
Microscopic analysis proved the skull came from the Lytle Member of the Purgatoire Formation, not the Morrison Formation.
James Kerr found the partial ornithopod skull at Garden of the Gods park in 1878. O.C. Marsh first identified it in 1886 as Camptosaurus amplus, a view later affirmed by Gilmore in 1909.
The original description viewed the animal as an intermediate form between Camptosaurus and Iguanodon.
Later cladistic analyses from 2010 and 2011 placed it as a basal member of Styracosterna, with Hippodraco as its closest relative.
This dinosaur lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago during the Aptian to Albian stages.
